question: In asymmetric intrauterine growth retardation, the typical ultrasound finding that reflects the fetal brain-sparing response is:

answers.text: Proportionate reduction in head circumference and abdominal circumference

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Proportionate reduction of all biometric parameters describes symmetric IUGR, which results from early-onset insults affecting cell number.

answers.text: Abdominal circumference disproportionately reduced relative to head circumference

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In asymmetric IUGR, placental insufficiency redistributes cardiac output to the brain (brain sparing): HC is relatively preserved while AC falls as hepatic glycogen and subcutaneous fat are depleted.

answers.text: Head circumference disproportionately reduced relative to abdominal circumference

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A disproportionately small head relative to abdomen would suggest a neurological or chromosomal cause, not the typical placental insufficiency pattern of asymmetric IUGR.

answers.text: Increased amniotic fluid index with reduced fetal movements

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Asymmetric IUGR typically produces oligohydramnios (reduced AFI), not increased amniotic fluid. Increased AFI would suggest a different aetiology.

overallFeedback.feedback: Asymmetric IUGR shows AC more reduced than HC (brain-sparing). Symmetric IUGR affects all parameters equally. Review the pathophysiology section for the mechanisms.
Well reasoned. Asymmetric IUGR: brain-sparing → HC preserved, AC reduced. Doppler showing absent/reversed end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery is a sign of severe uteroplacental insufficiency.
